The servant is identified here by the common noun 'my servant', a spare designation this row does not expand; the identity behind it is not decided by this row, whether an individual, a prophetic office, or a corporate referent. This row argues its four-verse bound from the sustained justice-noun thread and the fresh divine-speech-frame onset noted above, not from any external labeling of the passage. Two devices cross this unit's seams without disturbing the bound: the presentative הֵ֤ן, opening הֵ֤ן עַבְדִּי֙ (oshb:Isa.42.1, tier: byte), answers its counterpart at oshb:Isa.41.29 at accent_stripped tier across the opening seam; and the earth-noun בָּאָ֖רֶץ (oshb:Isa.42.4, tier: byte) shares only its stem with רֹקַ֥ע הָאָ֖רֶץ (oshb:Isa.42.5, tier: byte) across the closing seam, the attested tokens themselves returning tier NONE.

Neither device disturbs the cut: the speaker shifts from the trial-speech verdict on the idols to a third-person divine presentation of a new figure, and the parashah PE mark corroborates that shift, so the two continuity threads are disclosed as texture across the seam rather than as evidence against the boundary.
